The <b>EHDS Compliance Matrix</b> shows: The EHDS Compliance Matrix shows the approval chain status for every dataspace participant. Under Regulation (EU) 2025/327, secondary use of health data requires a complete chain:
<b>Access Application</b> · the data use: Access Application · the data user applies with purpose, justification and ethics assessment (Art. 67)
<b>HDAB decision</b> · the health data a: HDAB decision · the health data access body assesses the Art. 68(1) criteria and issues or refuses a data permit within three months (Art. 68)
<b>Dataset Grant</b> · the permit names: Dataset Grant · the permit names the dataset it grants access to (Art. 68(3))
<b>Contract</b> · the data user accesses: Contract · the data user accesses the data only under that permit, in a secure processing environment (Art. 61(1), Art. 73)
<b>Decision due:</b> the date by which t: Decision due: the date by which the access body must issue or refuse the data permit: three months after it received the application (Art. 68(4)). Late means the body has done neither by that date. The applicant may not access any data until it decides (Art. 61(1)), and the application and the decision must be published (Art. 57(1)(j)). The delay is the access body's compliance issue, not the applicant's.
Click a row for the application and the: Click a row for the application and the chain. Signed in as the access body, the row also carries the decision: a refused or missing permit blocks the transfer in step 5.

Your role cannot read the trust centre r: Your role cannot read the trust centre register. It is open to trust centre operators and the dataspace administrator; whether a health data access body may read it is still to be decided.

In November 2026 the Commission publishe: In November 2026 the Commission published the draft rules that every secure processing environment must follow from 26 March 2029 (EHDS Art. 73(5)). This page lists them in plain words and shows what this demo does about each one. The demo holds synthetic data only: green means the mechanism works here, not that a real operator is compliant.
A separate instance for each data permit: A separate instance for each data permit, cut off from other instances and networks, set up as the permit says.
One confidential workspace per data hold: One confidential workspace per data holder, not yet one per permit.
A separate staging area where holders an: A separate staging area where holders and users import data and code, checked and prepared by the access body first.
Holders' data arrives encrypted and its: Holders' data arrives encrypted and its fingerprint is part of the permit; there is no staging area for users yet.
Before access and throughout the permit,: Before access and throughout the permit, verify that the instance and its tools match the permit.
The processor's signed report must match: The processor's signed report must match the permit's policy hash before the key is released, again at every start.
Only the persons named in the permit get: Only the persons named in the permit get in, through a secure interface, kept apart when one person holds several permits.
Access by role through the web interface: Access by role through the web interface; one key per workspace, not per permit.
Data-science and statistics tools, and t: Data-science and statistics tools, and tools to work together, inside each instance.
Query only: questions in plain language: Query only: questions in plain language or Cypher, answered with aggregates.
Nothing leaves without the access body's: Nothing leaves without the access body's approval, with automatic and manual checks that only non-personal data goes out.
Counts below 5 are hidden automatically;: Counts below 5 are hidden automatically; there is no export request and review yet.
When the permit ends, access stops at on: When the permit ends, access stops at once and the instance is deleted within six months, verifiably.
Data lives only in encrypted memory and: Data lives only in encrypted memory and is gone when a workspace stops; stopping is not yet tied to the permit's end.
Public documentation of how the requirem: Public documentation of how the requirements are met, and a public list of the tools offered.
Design, decisions and the operator's run: Design, decisions and the operator's runbook are public; there is no list of tools yet.
Tell users about outages and planned mai: Tell users about outages and planned maintenance.

Role-based access derived from the permi: Role-based access derived from the permit, unique identities and strong authentication for every user.
Roles from the identity provider and EUD: Roles from the identity provider and EUDI Wallet sign-in; the demo's passwords are public on purpose.
Security management, incident reporting,: Security management, incident reporting, records of where data is hosted, and the power to stop processing at once.
Hosting region on record (West Europe) a: Hosting region on record (West Europe) and a stop button per workspace; no security management system, as befits a demo.
A third-party operator does not access t: A third-party operator does not access the personal data it hosts.
Confidential computing keeps the cloud o: Confidential computing keeps the cloud operator out of the workspace's memory; the key broker is run for the access body, still in the hub's own subscription.
Instances isolated from each other, data: Instances isolated from each other, data encrypted at rest and in transit.
Each workspace is its own confidential c: Each workspace is its own confidential container group; the extract is encrypted and every connection uses TLS.
An API with standard file types, documen: An API with standard file types, documentation, input validation, logging and versioning.
Documented, validated query API; no impo: Documented, validated query API; no import or export of files.
Batch jobs with the same output checks a: Batch jobs with the same output checks as interactive work, and a way to follow their status.
Queries run on demand with the same chec: Queries run on demand with the same checks; there is no queue for long jobs.
The access body can look into the enviro: The access body can look into the environment to supervise it and step in.
The access body sees attestation, polici: The access body sees attestation, policies and the audit chain.
Tamper-evident, write-once logs of sign-: Tamper-evident, write-once logs of sign-in, access, imports, processing, exports and administration.
A hash-chained audit log of attestation,: A hash-chained audit log of attestation, key release, loading and deletion; not yet in write-once storage.
Keep logs five years, or one year after: Keep logs five years, or one year after the permit ends if that is shorter.
Records of each instance's life, and int: Records of each instance's life, and internal and external audits.
Start, load and deletion of each workspa: Start, load and deletion of each workspace are on the audit chain; there is no audit programme.

One confidential workspace per data hold: One confidential workspace per data holder, not yet one per permit; the workspaces are reached over TLS on public addresses, not inside a private network.
